matches.description:
Adversaries may attempt to dump credentials to obtain account login and credential material, normally in the form of a hash or a clear text password. Credentials can be obtained from OS caches, memory, or structures.(Citation: Brining MimiKatz to Unix) Credentials can then be used to perform [Lateral Movement](https://attack.mitre.org/tactics/TA0008) and access restricted information.

Several of the tools mentioned in associated sub-techniques may be used by both adversaries and professional se

timeline.description: Windows Defender (MsMpEng.exe) accessed LSASS memory on workstation7, triggering Sysmon Event ID 10.

evidence.claim: The LSASS memory access event E042486 on workstation7 was generated by Windows Defender (C:\Program Files\Windows Defender\MsMpEng.exe), which is the legitimate built-in antimalware service performing routine scanning or monitoring.

next_actions: No further action required; close the alert as a false positive.
verdict.report_md:
## Incident Report: LSASS Process Memory Access (False Positive)

- **Verdict**: False Positive
- **Severity**: Low
- **Summary**: Alert R001-f1bba6fb triggered due to an LSASS process access event (Sysmon Event ID 10) on `workstation7`. Investigation revealed that the accessing process was `C:\Program Files\Windows Defender\MsMpEng.exe`, which is the legitimate Microsoft Defender antivirus service. This activity is expected behavior during routine security scans and does not represent credential dumping or malicious activity.
- **MITRE ATT&CK Techniques**: None (False Positive)
